note: Window agent p1630-p1639 (1 Nov 2026). Three kinds of fix: (1) compile unions every keyframe that covers a year, so a keyframe the dossier means 'for 1629-1631 only' (jesuit-reducciones_1629) or 'for 1804-1889' (wadai-empire_1636) keeps painting its full shape over the next keyframe; its from/to are restated here. (2) safavid-dynasty_1636 took Kandahar out of the Safavid shape in 1636, two years before the 1638 surrender; the ledger already removes it in 1638. (3) north-western Iraq (Mosul), grey (nobody) in 1630-1635 after the Ottoman ledger's 1625 loss, is Ottoman again from 1630 (events/0, rewritten by the reviewer on 2 Nov 2026 from a Safavid gain: the Mosul page keeps Mosul Ottoman before 1638 except 'a brief break in 1623').

region.text: the north-western Iraq that Cliopatria's 1626-1639 Ottoman shapes draw (Mosul, Erbil, Duhok and the Jazira side, with a strip of Salah ad-Din and Kirkuk), 297 of Iraq's 1,692 cells, which the Ottoman ledger lost in 1625 and no state holds

events.note: 1630: Mosul and north-western Iraq are Ottoman, 'an offensive platform for Ottoman campaigns into Iraq' while the Persians hold Baghdad. The Persians took 'most of Iraq, including the cities of Kirkuk and Mosul' after Baghdad fell in 1624, but on 4 July 1626 'the Ottoman army lifted the siege and withdrew to Mosul' (war page); the Mosul page has Persian rule only as 'a brief break in 1623, when Persia seized the city', and before 1638 Mosul was 'still a mere fortress, important for its strategic position as an offensive platform for Ottoman campaigns into Iraq'. The Ottoman ledger's 1625 loss (all Iraq outside Baghdad) left this land to nobody (grey 1626-1635) although Cliopatria's 1626 and 1636 Ottoman shapes keep it. Placed at the start of the window; the 9 Kirkuk cells follow Cliopatria (no page dates them). Reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: this replaces the window agent's Safavid gain of the same land, which the pages do not support for Mosul.

correction.text: for 1629-1631 only: the Cliopatria shape (with the Tapé missions of Rio Grande do Sul) plus Guayrá, which the bandeirantes raided from 1628; Guayrá drops out in 1632 (next keyframe)

keyframe_overrides.why: Same shape as the dossier's entry, with its stated span 1629-1631 made explicit: shapes.csv runs it to 1639 and the compiler unions overlapping keyframes, so it repainted Guayrá and Itatín (777 cells) over the 1632 keyframe. 'By the year 1632, 12,000 Guarani had been forcibly moved south, leaving the Guayrá region virtually deserted.'

correction.text: The Cliopatria 1636 shape unchanged, applied for 1804-1889

keyframe_overrides.why: Same shape and text as the dossier's entry, with the span its text gives (1804-1889) made explicit: shapes.csv starts it in 1636, which unioned the 280,000 km2 outline over the 1635 heartland keyframe (+606 cells). The page: 'In 1635, the Maba and other small groups in the region rallied to the Islamic banner of Abd al-Karim'; the growth is Sabun's: 'In 1805 Wadai conquered Bagirmi' and 'Sabun further extended his rule south to Dar Sila and Dar Runga'.
